correctness.rationale: For any finite FIR history, \(p_a(z)=z^{H-1}(L(z)-a)\), where \(L(z)=z-\sum_{j=0}^{H-1}k_jz^{-j}\). If all characteristic polynomials have roots in a disk of radius \(R<t/2\), the Laurent map omits the entire drift segment outside that disk. Composition with the inverse Joukowski map of the slit plane, followed by inversion, yields a disk self-map with \(g(0)=0\) and \(g\prime(0)=t/(2R)>1\), contradicting Schwarz lemma. At equality \(R=t/2\), its equality case forces \(g(\zeta)=\zeta\), hence \(L(z)=z+c+t^2/(4z)\), which uniquely determines every feedback coefficient. The explicit constructed quadratic factor has discriminant \((a-c)^2-t^2\le0\) and all nonzero roots of modulus \(t/2\) across the entire interval; the static case is an exact endpoint norm identity. The argument handles every finite \(H\) and every allowed drift; computational checks are supplementary and not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper constructs a one-lag stabilizer for two discrete scalar drifts and studies policy gradient, not an exact minimax rate for the full drift interval and all history lengths. The derived interval theorem includes the unique optimal coefficients for every history length and a conformal-map obstruction proving memory saturation. Classical interval-Schur and simultaneous-stabilization publications cover broader decision frameworks, but the accessible inspected material did not establish the same specialized sharp minimax/rigidity statement. The unresolved full-text comparison with the 1990 interval-Schur paper is explicitly retained as a material residual risk; mathematical novelty has not been equated with a failed search.

value.rationale: The 2026 FIR-LQR work uses history expansion to enable joint stability for sampled plants but leaves an exact interval-wide robust memory benefit unexplained. This theorem quantifies the sharp gain from one delayed observation, proves complete saturation for every larger finite-memory class, gives the unique optimal feedback, and doubles the exact admissible uncertainty-width threshold. It resolves a natural robust controller architecture decision by a nontrivial complex-analytic extremal obstruction rather than rephrasing the given two-plant example.
